roster.name: Xuna Kor'larym
roster.notes: Grew up in the Underdark; mother Nezia (family head), father Aki (a wizard), two older sisters and a younger brother. Fell in love with the stars the first time she left the caves; the family moved nearer the surface when she was 40, and at 60 she began studying the stars in libraries of manors, castles and study halls. She's seen the stars from peaks, trees and towers, and has come to the sea for an uninterrupted sky. Wild Shape forms, beast stat blocks and full text: see her sheet (Files).

inv.text: Star Map (a crystal on her necklace)

roster.persona:
Traits: seeks out the best place to view the stars (the crow's nest, the rigging). Collects small, beautiful things that catch her eye: shells, sea glass, anything glittery that reminds her of the stars.
Ideals: Wonder (the stars are beautiful and unreachable; she'd rather look up in awe than pretend to be world-wise). Perspective (the stars are proof there's good and beauty in the world, shining brighter in the dark).
Bond: her mother Nezia, the family head. They love snacks and chess together.
Flaw: when the stars are out, they have her attention, whatever she was supposed to be doing (sometimes even while trancing).
roster.looks: Drow, 100 years old, 5'8". Charcoal-gray skin, pale violet eyes, long white hair worn loose with small braids and shells braided in. Flowing layered clothes in shades of blue, hide armor over them, sturdy boots, a leather belt and pouch. Her star map hangs on a simple necklace: an oblong crystal engraved with stars.

regions.name: Home Waters
regions.notes: The coast around Kalatecha. Charted and patrolled.

regions.name: The Southern Reefs
regions.notes: Reefs, wrecks, and the false light of Lantern Rock.

regions.name: Uncharted
regions.notes: Everything the crew hasn't mapped yet.

nodes.name: Kalatecha
nodes.notes: The free city-state where every voyage begins and ends. Open its plan for the streets.

nodes.name: Lantern Rock
nodes.notes: A lonely island whose lighthouse has shone every night for as long as anyone remembers, though no one lives there. About two days' sail south. Ships that follow its light don't come back. The first island (2 to 3 sessions). Example fight at the lighthouse: six wreckers, two wrecker bruisers and the pirate queen (all in the library), built for level 3.

nodes.name: Ship Graveyard
nodes.notes: The lagoon full of wrecks on Lantern Rock. A giant octopus lives in the biggest one. A young stowaway who survived a wreck hides here. Example fight: one giant octopus, a minor fight at level 3.

nodes.name: The Sallowmay
nodes.notes: The captain's ship. She sails with the crew: in Build mode, drag her along as they go. Enter her for the deck, the captain's quarters and below decks.

shapes.name: The Open Sea
shapes.notes: Open water west and south of the coast. Uncharted beyond the home waters.
The reef that wrecks ships following the false light. The crew's job is to chart a safe channel through it.
The island itself: cliffs, a ship graveyard lagoon, sea caves, and the lighthouse.

regions.name: Harbor District
regions.notes: Piers, the warehouses, the fish market, the Drowned Bell, and the chandlery. Rowdy after dark.

regions.name: Old Town
regions.notes: The waterfront market, the Charter House, the cathedral, and the lookout hill. Busy by day.

regions.name: Upper Town
regions.notes: Villas on the terraced hills. Rich sponsors, and Hargrove-Vance.

regions.name: The Admiralty
regions.notes: The stone sea fortress on the northern headland. Armored guards, the harbormaster, and the city's cells.

regions.name: Outside the City
regions.notes: Farms and olive groves inland. The roads get lonely.

nodes.name: The Admiralty
nodes.notes: The stone sea fortress on the northern headland. Commodore Isadora Quell, the harbormaster: iron-gray braid, never sits. Her registry shows all three lost ships last logged a course past Lantern Rock. Her warning: "No ship has returned from the Ashen Isles." The city cells are here. Caught stealing: 5 gp fine or a night in the cells.

bmap.name: The Admiralty
bmap.notes: Commodore Quell's sea fortress: the guard room, her office, the registry of every ship (all three lost ships last logged a course past Lantern Rock), and the city cells. Caught stealing: 5 gp or a night in a cell.

nodes.name: Watchtower
nodes.notes: The round tower at the tip of the headland. Guards watch every ship that comes and goes.

nodes.name: The Drowned Bell
nodes.notes: Sailors' tavern in the old warehouses, run by Marisol Ferro, who calls everyone "minnow." One wall lists ships that never came home; the newest are the Heron, the Marigold, and the Silver Tern, all lost near Lantern Rock this year. Fish stew 4 cp, cider 2 cp. Sea shanty contest, arm wrestling, liar's dice.

bmap.name: The Drowned Bell
bmap.notes: Marisol's tavern. The bar runs down the west side with the casks behind it and the kitchen past it; the names of ships that never came home cover the north wall. Shanty contest on the little stage; stairs up to the rooms.

nodes.name: Fish Market
nodes.notes: Loud, wet, and smelly. Gulls everywhere. A good place for random event 1 (Admiral steals something) or 5 (a sea shanty breaks out).

bmap.name: The Fish Market
bmap.notes: Loud, wet and smelly: fish laid out on tables, tanks of live catch, and gulls everywhere. Open to the quay on the south side.

nodes.name: Benedetti's Chandlery
nodes.notes: In the last warehouse at the head of the harbor. Rope, lanterns, tar, and weapons on the back wall. Dario Benedetti, fussy, tape measure around his neck. The Sallowmay has never once come in for repairs, "not in all my thirty years."

nodes.name: The Charter House
nodes.notes: Grand arched building facing the head of the harbor across the plaza. Guild of Explorers headquarters: maps on every wall and a great half-blank globe. Michael Fontaine gives the Lantern Rock commission here (Scene 4). Buy old maps; sell new ones.

bmap.name: The Charter House
bmap.notes: The Guild of Explorers: maps on every wall, half of each one empty, and the great half-blank globe in the middle. Michael Fontaine's office is in the corner.

nodes.name: The Cathedral
nodes.notes: Great dome and tall bell tower, right behind the Charter House. Sister Amara Bellweather heals for a donation, sells Potions of Healing (50 gp), and blesses voyages (5 gp: reroll one d20 on the first voyage).

bmap.name: The Cathedral
bmap.notes: The great domed cathedral: rows of pews, pillars down the nave, the altar under the dome. The bell tower stands beside it (its own place); Sister Amara's infirmary is through the east door.

nodes.name: Bell Tower
nodes.notes: Pip Salazar, the half-deaf bell-ringer, swears the bells rang by themselves the morning the Sallowmay's crew notice went up.

nodes.name: Sister Amara's Infirmary
nodes.notes: Healing for anyone who's hurt, for whatever donation they can afford.

bmap.name: Sister Amara's Infirmary
bmap.notes: Sister Amara's infirmary: cots for the sick, shelves of herbs and potions (Potion of Healing 50 gp), and the oven where she bakes bread for the poor.

nodes.name: Market Square
nodes.notes: The market spills right along the east quay: fruit and spice stalls, crates, carts, and curio sellers (roll on the d10 curio table) beside the moored ships. Every merchant says the Sallowmay's supplies are "already settled." Scenes 2 and 3 happen here.

bmap.name: The Market Square
bmap.notes: The market square, loud and bright: stalls of fruit, spice and curios, the fountain in the middle. The cathedral's shadow falls across half of it; Old Tobias Pell's salvage stall is in the corner (Scenes 2 and 3).

nodes.name: Tobias's Stall
nodes.notes: At the edge of the square, in the cathedral's shadow. Old Tobias Pell sells salvage, including the lantern that burns without oil (10 gp). Admiral, his one-eyed gull, steals anything shiny.

nodes.name: Madame Zisa's Tent
nodes.notes: Fortunes read from tide shells, 1 silver each. "You will follow a light that lies. Trust the one that doesn't."

nodes.name: The Sallowmay
nodes.notes: Tied up at the end of the Long Pier. Every voyage begins and ends here. Captain Callomay never leaves her. Scrubbed deck, polished bronze fittings, not a scrap of iron. The crew-wanted notice is nailed to a post at the end of the pier.

nodes.name: The Undaunted
nodes.notes: Hargrove-Vance's ship, moored at the Merchant Pier. Fast, flashy, and in need of fresh paint. His deckhands loiter here between jobs.

nodes.name: Greta's Net Loft
nodes.notes: Greta Vasquez, retired bosun with a wooden leg, mends nets here and tells stories: "Never trust a light you didn't light yourself." Her grandmother called Lantern Rock's light "a light no human hand ever lit." Scene 5's dock fight happens along the quay out front.

nodes.name: Lookout Steps
nodes.notes: The hill on the south side of town. The city picture is the view from here: the harbor on the left, the fortress on the far headland, the cathedral dome, and the terraced hills on the right. Worn stone steps lead down to the quay, and armored guards often stand watch. A good spot to show the players the picture.

nodes.name: Moreau Villa
nodes.notes: Lady Celestine Moreau collects rare and wondrous things. She'd pay a fortune for "anything that glows" and offers 50 gold for the lantern.

bmap.name: Moreau Villa
bmap.notes: Lady Celestine Moreau's villa: a gallery of rare and wondrous things in glass cases, her salon, and a grand hall for parties. She'd pay 50 gold for the lantern.

nodes.name: Palm Terraces
nodes.notes: Terraced palm gardens high on the hill, with fountains and a view over the whole harbor. A good place to spot the Sallowmay, or the Undaunted, from above.

nodes.name: Hargrove House
nodes.notes: Rupert Hargrove-Vance's villa. The paint is peeling and the garden is overgrown, so he's broke, yet he still pays his crew. Snooping here can turn up a ledger of payments to "friends on the southern reefs."

bmap.name: Hargrove House
bmap.notes: Rupert Hargrove-Vance's villa: peeling paint, an overgrown garden, and still somehow the money to pay his crew. In the study, his ledger of payments to "friends on the southern reefs" (DC 15 to find).

nodes.name: Customs Post
nodes.notes: A toll booth where the Inland Road leaves town. Sergeant Bram Okoro of the City Guard often stands watch here.

bmap.name: The Customs Post
bmap.notes: Sergeant Okoro's post on the road out of town: a counter for tolls and papers, a small office, and one cell.

nodes.name: Under the Bridge
nodes.notes: Nico and Lina's hideout under the Inland Road bridge over the Brightwater. The twins know every alley, and they saw Hargrove-Vance's deckhands hiring toughs. They'll trade information for coins and sweets.

bmap.name: Under the Bridge
bmap.notes: Nico and Lina's hideout under the Inland Road bridge: bedrolls, a crate for a table, and their stash in a tin (they'll trade what they know for coins and sweets).

nodes.name: Olive Farm
nodes.notes: Farmland and olive groves inland. Not part of Session 1, but here if the players wander out the Inland Road.
Old stone warehouse on the north shore.
Old stone warehouse on the north shore.

nodes.name: Shipwright's Yard
nodes.notes: Slipways and timber stacks on the south shore. They build and mend every ship in the harbor, except the Sallowmay, which has never needed them.

bmap.name: The Shipwright's Yard
bmap.notes: Where ships are built and mended: a new hull on the slipway, stacks of timber, a crane, and the workshop. The Sallowmay has never once been here.

nodes.notes: Fishing boat.
Fishing boat.
Fruit and spice stall.
Curio stall. Roll on the d10 curio table.
Fish and bread stall.

nodes.name: Dockworkers' Shed
nodes.notes: Where the dock hands rest between ships. Ask here for work loading cargo, a few coppers a crate.

nodes.name: Dock Ambush (Scene 5)
nodes.notes: Where Hargrove-Vance's deckhands jump the crew on the way back to the ship. Sample fight: six deckhands, a Low warm-up for a level-3 party of four.

shapes.name: Kalatecha Harbor
shapes.notes: The harbor basin, sheltered by the fortress headland to the north. Open sea to the west.

shapes.name: Fortress Wall
shapes.notes: The Admiralty's walls run from the round watchtower east along the northern ridge, up into the terraced hills.

shapes.name: The Terraces
shapes.notes: Terraced hills with palms and villas, climbing behind the red-tiled rooftops. The Upper Town sits here.

shapes.name: Lookout Hill
shapes.notes: The hill the city picture is drawn from.

shapes.name: The Plaza
shapes.notes: The paved plaza between the head of the harbor and the Charter House.

shapes.name: Brightwater
shapes.notes: A small river that runs down from the inland hills, around the south side of Lookout Hill, and into the harbor.

shapes.name: The Quay
shapes.notes: The east quay. The dock fight in Scene 5 happens along here.

shapes.name: Long Pier
shapes.notes: The longest pier in the harbor.

shapes.name: The Steps
shapes.notes: Worn stone steps up to the lookout.

shapes.name: The Switchback
shapes.notes: A zigzag stair up the terraced hill.

shapes.name: Inland Road
shapes.notes: The road out of town toward the farms. It crosses the Brightwater on a stone bridge.

regions.name: The Sallowmay
regions.notes: The captain's ship, grown from a willow and a hawthorn. No innocent can be harmed aboard.

nodes.name: Captain's quarters
nodes.notes: His cabin at the stern. Roomier inside than it looks from the deck. The ship's log is on the desk; under the bunk, a sealed scallop shell. Searching it counts as prying if he finds out (he will).

bmap.name: The Sallowmay: captain's quarters
bmap.notes: His cabin, roomier inside than it looks from the deck: his bed under the stern windows, a side table and wardrobe, charts on the shelves, the desk with the ship's log on it, a small table for two, a sea chest. Three lamps. The ship's log is in the desk (DC 15); a sealed scallop shell is under the bed (DC 20).

nodes.name: Below decks
nodes.notes: Down the ladder through the hatch: the crew's hammocks, the galley (brick and bronze, no iron) and the hold. The masts run down through it to the keel.

bmap.name: The Sallowmay: below decks
bmap.notes: Below decks: the crew's hammocks, the galley (brick and bronze, no iron) with its table, the hold with crates, barrels and sacks, and the masts running down to the keel. No daylight reaches here: four lamps swing from the beams.

nodes.name: Main deck
nodes.notes: Scrubbed white, ropes coiled neat as sleeping snakes, every fitting bronze. The captain is usually at the rail, Thimble on his shoulder.

bmap.name: The Sallowmay: main deck
bmap.notes: The Sallowmay's main deck, scrubbed white, every fitting bronze. Lamps hang by the cabin door, at both masts, at the bow and by the hatch; the cabin door leads to the captain's quarters, the hatch down below decks.

docs.title: Session 1: Hired in Kalatecha
docs.md:
# Session 1: Hired in Kalatecha

Session 1 stays in Kalatecha and runs about 2 hours 20 minutes plus a break. It ends with the ship leaving the harbor at dusk. Everything has to happen in order, but any scene can shrink if you're running long. The fight in Scene 5 is the one to cut first.

Tick each part as you finish it. The run sheet at the top keeps the time, and the 📍 beside a part shows its place on the map; while this tab is open, every scene's place is numbered on the map. Read-aloud text is in the shaded boxes. Paraphrase it freely.

If you're running long at the break, play Scene 5 as a quick chase (about 10 minutes) instead of a fight.

## Before the players arrive

**Already settled:** the captain is [[npc:ln_callomay|Captain Callomay]] (true name Calandrous Callomaydare, DM only), with [[npc:ln_thimble|Thimble]] on his shoulder; his ship is the Sallowmay; the rival is [[npc:ln_hargrove|Rupert Hargrove-Vance]] of the Undaunted; the lantern seller is [[npc:ln_tobias|Old Tobias Pell]] and his gull Admiral. Rebekah is the navigator, Xuna Kor'larym.

- [ ] Everyone has a character. Only Xuna's sheet is in the Players folder so far; the others can be made now, or at the start of Scene 1
- [ ] Each character is on the Party tab, with full hit points
- [ ] An index card behind the screen with each player's name and a favor score of 0
- [ ] Graph or hex paper with only Kalatecha drawn in, ready for Rebekah as navigator
- [ ] A lantern prop: a battery tea light in a jar works
- [ ] A sealed letter from the Charter House holding the commission (Scene 4)
- [ ] A blank notebook for the ship's log
- [ ] The Dock Ambush is ready in the app for Scene 5: six of Hargrove-Vance's deckhands
- [ ] The Captain Callomay document on the Docs tab, in case anyone starts investigating him
- [ ] Snacks within reach, so the break is quick

## Opening {10 min} {place: kcity}

Put the city picture on the TV (top bar: **Players' screen** → Pictures → Show), or in the middle of the table, then read:

> The sun is warm on the red-tiled rooftops of Kalatecha, the free city by the sea. Tall-masted ships crowd the harbor, their sails patched with the colors of a dozen far-off ports. A stone fortress keeps watch over the coast. Above the market square, a great domed cathedral rises, and its bells ring out across the water.
> Kalatecha is where every voyage begins and ends. Sailors come home with strange spices, stranger stories, and maps of places no one has seen. Out past the horizon lie islands no one has charted: ruins, monsters, and peoples no one in Kalatecha has ever met.
> Each of you came to this harbor looking for a ship. This morning, one of them is looking for you.

Ask each player to point at one spot on the picture they'd like to visit someday. Remember their answers; they make good hooks for later sessions.

## Scene 1: Hired at the harbor {30 min} {place: kcity/psallow}

The captain hires the characters onto his ship, and each player takes a crew role. Start by reading:

> A notice is nailed to a post at the end of the longest pier, and the ink is still fresh. CREW WANTED. Honest hands for a voyage to uncharted waters. Ask aboard the Sallowmay.
> The Sallowmay sits at the end of the pier. She's not the biggest ship in the harbor, but she might be the best kept. Her deck is scrubbed white, her ropes are coiled neat as sleeping snakes, and every fitting gleams with polished bronze. A man leans on the rail at the top of the gangplank as if he's been waiting for you. On his shoulder sits a fairy no bigger than your hand, with dragonfly wings and a thimble for a helmet, looking you over as if you were fish at the market.

**Introductions.** Go around the table. Each player gives:

- Their character's name and what they look like.
- Why they need a ship. Are they after money, adventure, or getting away from something?

After each introduction, the captain asks that character one question from the rail. Pick from these or make up your own:

- "What's the farthest you've ever been from home?"
- "Can you swim?"
- "What would you do if you found a treasure no one could ever trace back to you?"
- "Do you keep your promises?" (Note what they say. It matters for the favor track.)

**The captain speaks.** Once everyone has introduced themselves:

> "Come aboard. I'm Captain Callomay." His eyes are the green of deep water, and his smile doesn't quite reach them. "The Sallowmay is mine, and she's the finest ship in Kalatecha, though I'm biased. What she lacks is a crew. I'll pay you a fair share of everything we earn and feed you better than any ship in this harbor. In return, you'll sail her."
> "One thing you should know. I don't go ashore, and I don't go exploring. I stay with the ship. Out there, the decisions are yours."
> The fairy on his shoulder sniffs. "He means me too. I'm Thimble. Don't call me his familiar."

If anyone asks for his full name, he smiles and says, "Captain Callomay will do." If anyone asks why he never leaves the ship, he says, "Someone has to keep her safe." Don't explain further. His true name is Calandrous Callomaydare. Never say it at the table. If they ask about Thimble, he answers truthfully: "People call her my familiar. She calls herself my conscience."

**Crew roles.** Rebekah's Xuna is already the navigator. Lay out the other three cards and let the rest choose. If two want the same role, let them sort it out, or have them roll a d20 for it. Write each role on the Party tab.

| Role | What they do | Good fit for |
| Medic | Keeps the crew alive and tends the sick and injured | Clerics, druids, anyone good at Medicine |
| Navigator | Reads stars and charts and draws the crew's map (Xuna) | Anyone good at Survival or with a high Wisdom or Intelligence |
| Quartermaster | Handles supplies, money, and trading | Bards, rogues, anyone with a high Charisma |
| Master-at-arms | Leads in battle and keeps the ship's weapons | Fighters, barbarians, paladins |

Hand Rebekah the blank map with Kalatecha drawn in. Hand the quartermaster the ship's purse.

**The ship.** The Sallowmay is her own place in the app. In DM mode, click her at the pier and press **Enter the Sallowmay**: inside are the [[place:kship/sdeck|Main deck]], the [[place:kship/squarters|Captain's quarters]] and [[place:kship/shold|Below decks]], and each one's **Enter this place** opens its map. Use them to show the crew around their new home, and for any fight aboard later. Anyone who searches the captain's quarters (they shouldn't, yet) can find the ship's log (DC 15) and, under the bunk, a sealed scallop shell (DC 20).

**Clue to drop.** When a player looks around the ship, describe the bronze: belaying pins, cleats, and the hilt of the captain's sword are all bronze. There isn't a scrap of iron anywhere on deck. Mention it once and move on.

**Send them ashore.**

> "We'll need supplies before we sail, and the Guild of Explorers has sent word that they have work for the Sallowmay. Go to the market, then to the Charter House. Bring back what we need, and bring me back whatever you hear."

**Favor watch.** This is the first chance to mark favor. Thanking him or complimenting the ship earns a +1 at the end of the night. Being rude to him earns a −1. Being rude to Thimble counts too; she tells him.

## Scene 2: The market {20 min} {place: kcity/ptobias}

The crew buys supplies and finds the lantern that burns without oil. Read:

> The market square is loud and bright. Stalls spill over with oranges, figs, and sacks of red and yellow spice. Gulls wheel overhead, waiting for someone to drop a fish. The cathedral's shadow falls across half the square, and in the cool of it, merchants sell things from far away: carved shells, feathered masks, a stuffed lizard as long as a rowboat.

**Supplies.** When the quartermaster tries to pay for food, rope, or water, every merchant waves the money away: "Already settled. Your captain's account." No one remembers him coming ashore to settle it. This is the second clue. Let it hang. (DM only: Thimble did it this morning, invisible. A player who makes a DC 15 Perception check spots a glint of dragonfly wings above the spice stall, gone in a blink.)

**The merchant.** At the edge of the square, in the cathedral's shadow, [[npc:ln_tobias|Old Tobias Pell]] sells salvage: coils of wet rope, a cracked compass, a figurehead with no face. He is a jumpy little man with a one-eyed gull named Admiral on his shoulder, and Admiral steals anything shiny. If anyone flashes a coin, Admiral grabs it and Tobias apologizes for him. Read:

> On a square of old sailcloth sits a brass lantern, its glass crusted with salt and tiny barnacles. Inside, a small flame burns a bright, steady gold. There's no wick and no oil. The flame just floats there, warm as a hand on your cheek.

Tobias wants 10 gold pieces for [[loot:ll_lantern|the lantern]] and won't say where it came from. He gets nervous if they press him. Let the players poke at it:

| Check | DC | What they learn |
| Insight | 10 | He keeps glancing toward the docks. He's scared of someone, not of the crew. |
| Investigation | 12 | The salt and barnacles mean it's been underwater for weeks. It came off a wreck. |
| Arcana | 12 | This isn't ordinary magic. The flame feels alive, and it always leans the same way, south, no matter how the lantern is turned. |
| Persuasion | 12 | He admits it came from a wreck on the southern reefs, sold to him by "people you don't want to meet." That's all he'll say. |

**Haggling.** A quartermaster who makes a DC 12 Persuasion check gets it for 5 gold pieces. If the crew is kind to Tobias and short of money, he'll let it go cheap just to be rid of it.

## Scene 3: The rival {15 min} {place: kcity/ptobias}

The rival explorer tries to take the lantern out from under the crew. Start just as the crew is about to buy it. Read:

> The crowd parts for a lean, silver-haired man in a fine Guild coat with the badges picked off. A monocle glints in one eye, and a leather journal is tucked under his arm. Two broad-shouldered deckhands follow close behind. "Well, well." Rupert Hargrove-Vance doesn't look at you, only at the lantern. "Merchant, I'll give you twenty gold for that, and you can forget you ever had it."

**What [[npc:ln_hargrove|Hargrove-Vance]] does.**

- Offers double whatever the crew offers, up to 30 gold pieces.
- Talks down to the crew: "A ship full of new hires? How sweet. Does your captain let you hold the wheel?"
- Boasts about sailing first: "The Undaunted sails at dawn. Wherever that trinket came from, I'll be there before you've finished packing."
- Opens his journal and reads aloud: "Day one. New crew of the Sallowmay. Already overpaying for junk." He writes down every mistake they make, and says it out loud as he writes.

**His magic, just a glimpse.** He's a real warlock, and he doesn't want anyone to know it here. Give the table one odd detail and nothing more: the pages of his journal turn by themselves in a wind no one else feels, or Admiral shrieks and won't go near him. A player who makes a DC 15 Arcana check feels fae magic on him, cold and sharp, nothing like the captain's. (DM only: his familiar, a sprite, rides invisible on his collar. If Thimble is with the crew, she hisses at the empty air there.)

**Who gets the lantern.** Tobias sells to whoever treated him better, and the rival is rude to him. If the crew has been decent at all, he sells to them. If the rival does end up with it, the deckhands are carrying it in Scene 5, and the fight becomes about getting it back.

**As the rival leaves,** describe a look between the rival and the two deckhands. A player who makes a DC 12 Insight check catches it: the rival isn't done.

**Why the rival wants it (DM only).** He buys loot from the wreckers on Lantern Rock. This lantern slipped through and ended up in the market, and he wants it back before anyone traces it to the reef. Since the Guild stopped favoring him, that loot is how he pays for the Undaunted. There's more: his patron, an Unseelie fae, wants Captain Callomay to lose his wager, so the Sallowmay's crew must never finish a chart. Stopping this crew is his real job. The players can piece this together over many sessions.

## Snack break {15 min}

Good stopping point: the crew has the lantern and knows it has a rival.

## Scene 4: The Charter House {15 min} {place: kcity/pcharter}

[[npc:ln_fontaine|Michael Fontaine]] hires the ship to chart Lantern Rock. Read:

> The Charter House of the Guild of Explorers is a grand building of pale stone with tall arched windows. Inside, every wall is covered in maps, and half of every map is empty. In the middle of the hall stands a huge globe. The parts no one has explored are painted with sea serpents.
> A tall, blond man in his early thirties hurries over. He's holding a stack of papers and has ink on his fingers. "You must be the new crew of the Sallowmay. Michael Fontaine, Guild of Explorers. Your captain's letter came this morning, so he's already said yes. Come, come."

**Another odd detail.** If anyone asks who delivered the captain's letter, Fontaine frowns: "It was on my desk when I came in. I assumed one of the clerks…" (DM only: Thimble, through the window. There's a tiny wet footprint on the sill, smaller than a mouse's.)

**When he sees the lantern,** he stops cold and lowers his voice:

> "Where did you get that? No, never mind. That's exactly why I asked for you." He unrolls a chart. Far to the south, a small island is circled in red. "Lantern Rock. There's a lighthouse on it that has shone every night for as long as anyone remembers, and no one lives there. Ships that follow its light don't come back. We've lost three this year."

**The commission.** Hand over the sealed letter prop. On the TV, switch back to the map and un-hide [[place:klantern|Lantern Rock]] (and the reef around it) so it appears on the sea chart as Fontaine unrolls his chart. The Guild offers:

- 50 gold pieces each to chart a safe channel through the reef and find out what happened to the lost ships.
- A bonus for anything valuable they bring back.
- A copy of the Guild's chart. Have Rebekah draw Lantern Rock onto the crew's map, about two days' sail south. The reef around it stays blank.

A quartermaster who makes a DC 15 Persuasion check raises the fee to 60 gold pieces each.

**If they ask Fontaine questions:**

- **Why us?** "Nobody else will take it. Well, Hargrove-Vance has been asking about Lantern Rock all week, which worries me."
- **Who is Hargrove-Vance?** "He was the Guild's best explorer, once. He thinks we owe him every job worth having. We don't."
- **Has the Guild sent anyone?** "One ship, two months ago, the Heron. She never came back."
- **Is it magic?** "I sit behind a desk now. Ask me about paperwork."
- **Why did he stop adventuring?** "I used to do this, you know. Then I discovered chairs."

## Scene 5: Trouble on the docks {25 min} {place: kcity/pambush}

Hargrove-Vance's deckhands try to take the lantern as the crew heads back to the ship. Read:

> The docks are busy with the end of the day's work. Cranes swing cargo nets overhead, crates are stacked higher than your heads, and the Sallowmay is just in sight at the end of the pier. Then three figures step out from behind the crates ahead, and three more behind you. You recognize the rival's deckhands. "We'll take that lantern," says one. "No need for anyone to get wet."

**The fight.** Use the [[place:kcity/pambush|Dock Ambush]] in the app: six of [[foe:lf_deckhand|Hargrove-Vance's deckhands]], built on the SRD Tough stat block. Its battle map is the docks: the pier to the Sallowmay, the crane with its rope and cargo net, two stacks of crates where the deckhands hide, a fish cart, and the warehouses behind. Everyone starts in place: the crew on the quay, three deckhands at the crates ahead and three at the crates behind. That's a Low fight for four level-3 characters under the 2024 rules: a warm-up. Keep it fast:

- The deckhands want the lantern, not a killing. If a character drops to 0 hit points, the deckhands grab the lantern and run instead of finishing them.
- When two deckhands are down, or when the crew has the lantern safe, the rest flee. Mark them Fled in the app.
- Let the master-at-arms decide whether to chase them.

**Things to use on the docks.** Reward players who use the scenery:

| Action | Check | Result |
| Swing on a crane's rope | Athletics or Acrobatics, DC 10 | Land anywhere on the dock, and get advantage on the next attack |
| Topple a stack of crates | Athletics, DC 12 | Everyone under it is knocked prone |
| Shove someone off the pier | Athletics against their Athletics or Acrobatics | They're in the water and out of the fight for a round |
| Drop a cargo net | Dexterity, DC 12 | One deckhand is tangled and can't move until they get free |

**Quick-chase version (10 minutes).** If time is short, skip the fight. One deckhand snatches the lantern and runs. The crew needs two successes out of three:

- Leap a fish cart: Athletics, DC 12.
- Cross a narrow gangplank: Acrobatics, DC 12.
- Spot the deckhand in the crowd: Perception, DC 12.

If they fail, the deckhand drops the lantern off the pier as he escapes. Someone has to dive in after it: Athletics, DC 10. Underwater, the lantern is still burning.

**Afterward.** Give the medic a chance to patch up the crew. Anyone who searches a fallen deckhand rolls Wisdom (Perception) in the app: each one carries the five silver he was paid, and one has [[loot:ll_hvnote|a note signed H.V.]] in his pocket (DC 10). A captured deckhand talks if treated well: "Hargrove-Vance paid us five silver each. Said it wasn't worth the trouble anyway."

## Scene 6: Set sail {10 min} {place: kcity/psallow}

The crew returns to the ship, and the Sallowmay leaves the harbor at dusk. The captain is at the rail when they come back. He asks what happened, and he listens closely if they mention the rival. Telling him the truth earns favor. Thimble wants every detail of the fight, and takes the side of whoever told it best.

Go around the table and ask each player for one thing their character does as the ship casts off. Some ideas by role:

- **Navigator:** Xuna sets the course south and pins the map to the chart table.
- **Quartermaster:** stows the supplies and counts the purse.
- **Medic:** sets up a sick bay below deck.
- **Master-at-arms:** checks the ship's weapons and keeps an eye on the Undaunted.

Then read:

> The sails fill and the Sallowmay slides away from the pier. Behind you, Kalatecha glows gold in the setting sun. Then the cathedral bells begin to ring. People on the docks stop and look up. It's not the evening hour, and it's not a pattern anyone in the city has heard before.
> At the rail, Captain Callomay closes his eyes and smiles as if the bells were meant for him.
> On the chart table, the lantern's little flame leans south, toward a lighthouse no one tends and a reef no one has crossed. Lantern Rock is waiting.

End the session there.

**The ship's log.** Ask who wants to keep the ship's log. That player writes a few lines tonight or before next session, and you'll read it aloud to open Session 2.

## After the session

- [ ] Update each player's favor score on the index card. Note what raised or lowered it.
- [ ] Write down the spot each player pointed at on the city picture.
- [ ] Write down any names, promises, or details the players made up (the Notes tab works).
- [ ] Note who has the lantern and how much gold they spent.
- [ ] Ask the players what they liked best, and do more of it.
- [ ] Data tab: Download survey.json, and put it in the campaign folder's Saves folder.

**Session 2** opens with the ship's log, then the voyage south and the first scene on Lantern Rock: the false light.

# Reference

### Spotlight tracker

Each player should get at least one moment tonight where their choice changes what happens.

- [ ] Navigator (Rebekah, Xuna): reads the lantern's flame in the market, or draws Lantern Rock onto the map
- [ ] Medic: patches up the crew after the docks, or wins over a captured deckhand
- [ ] Quartermaster: haggles for the lantern, or raises Fontaine's fee
- [ ] Master-at-arms: leads the dock fight and decides whether to chase

### Quick rules reference

| Situation | Rule |
| How hard is a check? | Easy DC 10, medium DC 15, hard DC 20 |
| Something helps or hurts | Advantage: roll two d20s and take the higher. Disadvantage: take the lower. |
| A character drops to 0 hit points | Death saving throws each turn: a d20 roll of 10 or higher is a success. Three successes and they're stable; three failures and they die. |
| A natural 20 on a death save | They regain 1 hit point |
| A natural 1 on a death save | Counts as two failures |
| A character dies | The captain's safety net: see "The rescue and the reveal" in the Captain Callomay document |

# Age of Exploration Campaign Notes

Oct 5, 2026 · @Joseph Crook

## Campaign overview

The crew sails out from Kalatecha, a bustling port city-state, to explore uncharted islands, mapping the unknown and bringing back treasure and stories. Each island is its own adventure; the city ties them together.

- **System:** Dungeons & Dragons, in an original setting built by the DM.
- **Players:** the DM's girlfriend (27), her brother (15), and her sisters (13 and 11). The three siblings have played about three sessions before; this is the DM's first campaign.
- **Tone:** swashbuckling adventure and mythical wonder. Islands are ruins, monster lairs, or home to peoples the crew trades and allies with — not lands to conquer.
- **Structure:** sail out, explore an island, come home to sell maps and resupply, repeat.
- **Table goals:** snappy combat, and every player gets a spotlight moment each session.

## The home port

Kalatecha is a sunny, walled harbor city-state where every voyage begins and ends. Tall-masted ships crowd the docks, a stone sea fortress guards the coast, and a great domed cathedral rises over a busy market square. Palm trees and terraced hills climb behind the red-tiled rooftops.

Show the players the city picture at the first session and let them point to where they want to go.

- **City name:** Kalatecha, an independent city-state.
- **City crest and flag:** set by the DM — the picture shows a real historical banner, so give the city its own.

## Key locations

Six places in the city, each with a job in the campaign. Names are placeholders.

| Location | Where in the picture | Role in the game | Hook or use |
| The Harbor | Docks, left side | Where the crew's ship is moored; every voyage starts and ends here | Overheard rumors, stowaways, suspicious cargo |
| The Admiralty | Stone sea fortress along the coast | Harbormaster tracks every ship; home of the armored city guards | Official warnings: "No ship has returned from the Ashen Isles" |
| The Charter House | Grand arched building on the plaza | Headquarters of the Guild of Explorers, who hire expeditions and buy new maps. Their goal: explore and turn a profit | A patron with a job starts each adventure |
| The Cathedral | Domed church with the tall bell tower | Main temple: healing, blessings before a voyage, a cleric NPC | Bells ring a special pattern when the crew's ship returns |
| The Market Square | Fruit and spice stalls in the plaza | Strange goods from distant islands turn up here | A merchant selling something no one can identify, like a lantern that burns without oil |
| The Upper Town | Villas on the terraced hills | Where wealthy sponsors live | Home of the rival explorer |

## Key NPCs

| NPC | Role | Description |
| Michael Fontaine | The crew's contact at the Guild of Explorers | Tall, blond, early 30s. A former adventurer who moved into middle management at the Guild because it's safer. |
| Captain Callomay | DM's NPC who owns and captains the crew's ship | A fully built character, a little higher level than the party. More part of the setting than an active adventurer: he hired the crew to sail his ship, never leaves it, and leaves the decisions to the crew rather than joining their exploits. The crew thinks he's a warlock with a fae patron; see the secret below. The crew knows him only as Captain Callomay. |
| Rupert Hargrove-Vance | Recurring rival from the Upper Town; captain of the Undaunted | A former Guild star who resents the Guild for handing its best jobs to newcomers like the crew. Wears a monocle and keeps a journal of every mistake the crew makes, which he reads aloud to them. Has a history with Michael Fontaine. Since the Guild stopped favoring him, buying the wreckers' loot is how he pays for the Undaunted. |

## DM only: the captain's secret

The crew believes the ship's captain is a warlock with a fae patron. In truth, he is the fae, and his true name is Calandrous Callomaydare. How each player treats him quietly shapes their luck, and they never see the score.

### Favor track

Keep a hidden score for each player from −3 to +3, starting at 0. Adjust it at the end of each session.

| Raises favor | Lowers favor |
| Thanking him for the ship or his hospitality | Mocking or insulting him |
| Including him in plans and celebrations | Ignoring him or bossing him around |
| Bringing him a gift or a share of treasure | Breaking a promise to him |
| Keeping their word | Lying to him |
| Asking about his story politely | Prying into his true name |

| Score | Secret effect |
| +3 | Once per session, a failed roll quietly becomes a success |
| +1 or +2 | Advantage on one roll per session, or a few temporary hit points after a long rest aboard |
| 0 | No effect |
| −1 or −2 | Disadvantage on one roll per session |
| −3 | One small mishap per session: a snapped rope, a spoiled ration, an ill wind |

### Clues to drop

- The ship never seems to need repairs, and no one ever sees him pay for supplies.
- He won't touch cold iron; his sword and the ship's fittings are bronze.
- He never gives his full name.
- Milk sours when he's annoyed, and flowers open when he's pleased.
- Sea creatures and seabirds that come near the ship treat him with odd respect.

### Running it

- Keep penalties mild and rewards generous, so the youngest player isn't punished for a joke.
- Let players notice the pattern on their own; never confirm it.
- Save the reveal for a big moment, such as when the crew stands up for him or badly betrays him.
- **Safety net:** if a character dies, especially the youngest player's, the captain appears out of thin air beside them and brings them back. It is the only time he ever leaves the ship, and that rescue doubles as the reveal. Use it only once, keep it open to any player, and consider a small fae price, like a favor owed or a silver mark on the skin.

## The crew and ship

The ship belongs to the captain, who hires the players as his crew: they run it and map the world from its deck.

- **Ship name:** the Sallowmay, the captain's ship.
- **Crew roles:** each player takes one of medic, navigator, quartermaster, or master-at-arms (the crew's fighter, who leads in battle and keeps the ship's weapons). The DM plays the ship's captain and patron, an NPC who owns the ship and hires the crew. He never leaves the ship and leaves the decisions to the crew. Roles give everyone a job and a reason to care about the ship.
- **The blank map:** hand the players graph or hex paper with only the home port drawn in. As they sail, they draw coastlines, name islands, and mark dangers.
- **Ship's log:** one player writes a few lines after each session; read it aloud to recap at the start of the next.

Role holders:

- [ ] Medic:
- [x] Navigator: Xuna Kor'larym (Rebekah)
- [ ] Quartermaster:
- [ ] Master-at-arms:
- [x] Ship's captain and patron (DM's NPC), name: Captain Callomay

## Session 1 plan

Session 1 stays in the city so the DM can find their footing and the players warm up with low stakes, and ends with the ship leaving the harbor.

- **Meet the crew.** Each player introduces their character. The captain hires them aboard his ship at the harbor, and each picks a crew role.
- **The market.** The crew explores the market square. A merchant has a strange item from an unknown island and won't say where it came from.
- **The rival.** A cocky rival explorer from the upper town shows up, wants the same item, and boasts about sailing first.
- **The job.** Michael Fontaine of the Guild of Explorers offers a commission: chart the island the item came from and bring back proof.
- **A small challenge.** A short scuffle on the docks or a chase through the market refreshes combat and ability checks.
- **Set sail.** End the night with the cathedral bells ringing as the ship leaves the harbor.

Aim for 2 to 3 hours with snack breaks. Give each player at least one moment where their choice changes what happens.

## The first voyage and beyond

The first island is an original one, built by the DM to fit the campaign's vibe and tied to the strange item from the market.

- **First island:** keep it small — a handful of locations, one or two fights, one mystery or puzzle, and a clear prize to bring home. It's the island the market item came from.
- **Coming home:** after each island, the crew returns to the home port to sell their map, heal, resupply, and pick up the next rumor.
- **Later islands:** Ghosts of Saltmarsh adds rules for ships, sailing, and naval combat, plus seafaring adventures to drop in as new islands or ports. It was written for the 2014 rules but works alongside the newer ones.
- **The rival explorer:** shows up every few islands, sometimes ahead of the crew, sometimes needing rescue. Gives the campaign a throughline without heavy plotting.
- **Island ideas to fill in:** ruins of a lost people, a monster's lair, a friendly island to trade with, a place that isn't on any map.

## First island: Lantern Rock

A lonely island whose lighthouse has shone every night for as long as anyone remembers, though no one lives there. Ships that follow its light don't come back. It should take 2 to 3 sessions.

**The secret.** The light is a firebird, a great flame-feathered bird locked in an iron cage at the top of the lighthouse. Wreckers led by a pirate queen use its light to lure ships onto the reef, then loot the wrecks. The rival explorer buys their loot, and now wants the firebird itself.

**The hook.** The merchant's strange item is a lantern that burns without oil, salvaged from a wreck on the reef. Three ships have vanished near Lantern Rock this year. Michael Fontaine hires the crew to chart a safe channel through the reef and find out what happened, with a bonus for anything valuable they bring back.

### Scenes

- **The false light.** Night falls as the ship nears the reef, and the lighthouse blazes to life. The navigator must trust the stars over the light; following it runs the ship onto the rocks. Failure means a scraped hull and a rough landing, not disaster.
- **The ship graveyard.** A lagoon full of wrecks to search for loot and clues. A giant octopus lives in the biggest one. A young stowaway who survived a wreck is hiding here and tells the crew about the wreckers.
- **Wreckers' Cove.** The pirates' camp sits in sea caves below the cliffs, with sailors from the lost ships held for ransom. The crew can sneak in, bluff, or fight.
- **The lighthouse.** A spiral stair climbs the cliff tower. At the top, the pirate queen and the rival are haggling over the caged firebird. Big swashbuckling fight on the stairs and in the lantern room: swinging from the great lamp's chains and knocking pirates off the gallery into the sea.
- **The choice.** The firebird can be freed or sold. The Guild would pay a fortune for it. Freed, it bursts into the sky, lights a safe path through the reef, and leaves the crew a feather that never stops glowing.
- **Escape.** With the cove in uproar, the crew gets the rescued sailors back to the ship while the rival slips away.

**The prize.** The first safe chart of the reef for the Guild, loot from the wrecks, grateful sailors with friends back in Kalatecha, and either a fortune or a firebird feather, depending on their choice.

### Spotlight moments

| Crew role | Their moment |
| Navigator | Trusts the stars over the false light and steers the safe channel through the reef/maps the island |
| Medic | Tends the rescued sailors, or soothes the injured firebird so it can fly |
| Quartermaster | Sorts out what's valuable in the wrecks, or bluffs the wreckers into a deal |
| Master-at-arms | Leads the charge up the lighthouse stairs and duels the pirate queen |

For monsters, look for giant octopus, pirate or bandit, and bandit captain stat blocks in the rules. The firebird doesn't need stats; it's a prize, not a fight.

## Materials checklist

- [ ] The D&D rules: the free rules on D&D Beyond, or the 2024 Player's Handbook
- [ ] A set of dice for each player
- [ ] Dry-erase battle mat and markers
- [ ] Graph or hex paper for the players' map
- [ ] Index cards and pencils
- [ ] DM screen (a standing folder works)
- [ ] Props: a tea-stained "old map," a sealed letter from the Charter House, a notebook for the ship's log
- [ ] Snacks
- [ ] Later: Ghosts of Saltmarsh
- [ ] Later: 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide

## Still to decide

- [ ] What's on Kalatecha's flag?
- [ ] Who leads the Guild of Explorers?
- [ ] What's the pirate queen's name?
- [ ] What does each player want their character to be?
- [ ] Date and length of session 1.

# Captain Callomay

Oct 7, 2026 · Joseph Crook

DM only. The captain of the Sallowmay, as the crew knows him and as he really is: his numbers for when the players start investigating him, what each kind of snooping turns up, and his story.

## At a glance

| **What the crew sees** | Captain Callomay, owner and captain of the Sallowmay. Lean and unhurried, eyes the green of deep water, a smile that doesn't quite reach them, a bronze-hilted sword. Courteous, dry, a little sad. A fairy named Thimble rides on his shoulder. Everyone assumes he's a warlock with a fae patron and that she's his familiar, and he lets them. |
| **What he really is** | An archfey: Calandrous Callomaydare, once called the Lord of Far Shores. The warlock is a costume. There is no patron. He is the fae. |
| **What he wants** | To pay off a wager he lost to the sea three hundred years ago, so he can stand on dry land again. |
| **What he fears** | That he'll outlive this crew too. And, quietly, that when he's finally free he'll miss the sea. |
| **Voice** | Unhurried and courteous. Calls the crew by their roles ("Navigator", "Medic") until they earn their names. Answers questions with questions when he'd rather not answer. |
| **Rules he can't break** | He never tells an outright lie. He can't set foot on land. He can't touch cold iron. He can't draw a map of a mortal coast. He keeps every bargain he makes, to the letter. |
| **The ship's rule** | No innocent can be harmed aboard the Sallowmay, and nothing innocent ends up on her table. The crew aren't covered: they're crew, not guests. See No innocents aboard. |

## His numbers

He never rolls to fight. Fights around him are narrative (see Running him in a fight). These numbers are for the moments the players test him: lying to him, sneaking past him, studying him. They're my homebrew numbers for an archfey, not a stat block from the rules.

| **Str** | **Dex** | **Con** | **Int** | **Wis** | **Cha** |
| 12 (+1) | 18 (+4) | 16 (+3) | 18 (+4) | 20 (+5) | 24 (+7) |

| **Proficiency bonus** | +6 |
| **Saving throws** | Dex +10, Wis +11, Cha +13; the rest use the ability modifier |
| **Skills** | Deception +19, Insight +17, History +16, Performance +13, Persuasion +13, Perception +11, Survival +11, Arcana +10, Sleight of Hand +10, Stealth +10 |
| **Passive Perception** | 21 |
| **Passive Insight** | 27 |
| **Senses** | On the Sallowmay he knows everything that happens aboard, as if the ship tells him. |
| **Languages** | Every language anyone has ever spoken at sea. He pretends not to understand some of them. |

## The warlock act

He never claims to be a warlock. Other people say it, and he doesn't correct them. Everything he says about it is true, just carefully worded:

> "People say I made a pact with a fae. I made a bargain, yes. I've been paying for it ever since."

> "Who do I serve? The sea. She's the oldest of them all. The sailors call her Mother Brine."

> "My price? Maps. Every true chart you draw takes a little off what I owe."

Small magic he does in plain view, which looks like a warlock's tricks: a lantern lights when he touches it, ropes knot themselves, a breeze comes when he whistles, fog parts in front of the bow, and spilled water runs back into its cup. He never needs to roll for any of it.

And every warlock story has a familiar, so the crew will assume Thimble is his. She isn't (see Thimble, below). Asked about her, he tells the truth:

> "People call her my familiar. She calls herself my conscience."

> "I don't command Thimble. I ask, and most days she says yes."

## Thimble, the fairy who isn't a familiar

A sprite no bigger than a hand: dragonfly wings, a sewing needle for a sword, a thimble for a helmet. Bossy, nosy and fiercely loyal. She calls the captain "Callo" and the crew "the new ones." She was part of his court in the old days, helped plant the willow and the hawthorn the Sallowmay grew from, and followed him to sea when he lost the wager. Nobody ordered her to.

**What she does for him.** He can't set foot on land, so Thimble goes ashore for him: she's his eyes on the docks, his ears in the taverns, and the one who brings back gossip. She can't draw maps any more than he can; fae ink won't hold a mortal coast. When he wants to know whether someone is honest, he asks Thimble, who has looked at their heart (her Heart Sight).

**Her numbers.** Use the SRD Sprite stat block; it's on her sheet in the app. AC 15, 10 hit points, speed 10 feet and fly 40 feet. Needle Sword (+6, 1d4 + 4 piercing). Enchanting Bow (+6, 1 piercing, and the target is Charmed until the start of her next turn). Heart Sight (a creature within 5 feet makes a DC 10 Charisma save or she learns its emotions and alignment). She can turn invisible at will. She counts as crew, not a guest, so the ship's rule doesn't protect her either.

**How she gives the game away.** A real familiar comes from the Find Familiar spell, and the spell sets rules she keeps breaking. Players who know the rules can catch it:

| **A real familiar (Find Familiar)** | **Thimble** |
| **A spirit wearing an animal's shape.** | A real fey, flesh and wings. |
| **Obeys its master's commands.** | Argues with him in front of everyone, and sometimes says no. |
| **Can't attack.** | Draws her needle sword on anyone who threatens him. |
| **At 0 hit points it disappears, dropping whatever it carried, until the spell is cast again.** | Hurt, she bleeds like anyone else. She doesn't vanish. |
| **Its master talks to it in their mind within 100 feet, and can see through its eyes.** | They talk out loud. She flies ashore for a whole day and reports back in person. |
| **Its master can send it away to a pocket dimension.** | When she wants to be gone, she just turns invisible. |

## When they investigate him

**He never lies, so don't roll his Deception against their Insight.** Instead, a good Insight check notices that he's dodging. That's the fun of it: the kids can learn that he's hiding something without learning what. His Deception matters when he's misleading someone in other ways, like a bluff to a stranger or a trick of wording.

| **They try to** | **Roll** | **What they learn** |
| **Catch him in a lie** | Wisdom (Insight), DC 15 | Success: "He's choosing his words very carefully. He answered a slightly different question than the one you asked." Failure: he seems completely sincere, which he is. |
| **Lie to him** | None | His passive Insight is 27; he always knows. He doesn't say so. Lying to him lowers favor, as in the campaign notes. |
| **Sneak or pickpocket on the ship** | Dex (Stealth or Sleight of Hand) vs his passive Perception 21 | The ship tells him. The first time, he finds it funny and returns what was taken. After that it counts as breaking his trust. |
| **Study his magic** | Intelligence (Arcana), DC 15 | A warlock's magic comes through a pact, and pacts leave a mark: a sigil, a token, a voice in their head. He has none, and the fairy on his shoulder isn't one either (see Study Thimble). "The magic doesn't come through him. It comes from him." DC 20: it's fae magic, older than any pact. |
| **Study Thimble** | Intelligence (Arcana), DC 15 | She's no familiar. A familiar is a spirit wearing a borrowed shape, and it does as it's told. Thimble is a real sprite, and she argues with him. DC 20: she's from a fae court, and she serves him the way a courtier serves a lord, by her own choice. |
| **Win Thimble over** | Charisma (Persuasion), DC 15 | She never tells his secret, but she lets one true thing slip: "I knew him when he had a garden." Call her his familiar and she's insulted: "I am not his pet. I'm his..." and she stops. No roll needed for that part. |
| **Cast Detect Magic on him** | None | Illusion magic clings to his face and hands (his human look is a glamour). The whole ship glows faintly too: hull, rigging and figurehead, but not the cargo or the crew's own things. |
| **Remember fae lore** | Intelligence (Arcana or Nature), DC 15 | Fae can't abide cold iron. They don't lie, but they twist words. Names hold power. A bargain with a fae binds both sides. DC 20: even fae can be bound, by bargains with powers older than they are. |
| **Search [[place:kship/squarters|his cabin]]** | Intelligence (Investigation), DC 15 | The ship's log, written in dozens of different hands, crew after crew, the oldest pages so faded the ink is nearly gone. Counts as prying if he finds out (he will). |
| **Search it thoroughly** | Intelligence (Investigation), DC 20 | Under the bunk, a sealed scallop shell. Inside, a strand of kelp tied in a knot that won't come undone. Arcana DC 20 recognizes it: a bargain, still binding. |
| **Dig through city records** | Intelligence (History), DC 15, or ask Commodore Quell | The Admiralty's registry lists the Sallowmay in every ledger back to the city's founding. The captain is always written down as "Captain C." |
| **Hand him something iron** | Wisdom (Insight), DC 10 | He declines it gracefully, but there's a flicker of real distaste, like someone offered a dead fish. |
| **Ask him about his story, politely** | None | He tells them a sea story: the warlock act above, or the tale of the wager told as if it happened to someone else. Raises favor, as in the campaign notes. |

**His true name.** No roll ever finds it; it comes out only in the reveal. If a player ever speaks it to him, he must answer one question with the plain truth. Unless it's used to help him, that player's favor drops to −3 for good.

## Running him in a fight

- **He doesn't join their fights.** The bargain counts only charts made by mortal choice, so he leaves the decisions, and the danger, to the crew.
- **If the ship is attacked,** the sea answers for him: a wave knocks boarders off the rail, the rigging tangles around an attacker, a sudden fog hides the ship. Use it to tip a fight, never to win it outright.
- **If someone attacks him,** blades pass through him like mist and spells unravel on his skin. He doesn't fight back. He's disappointed, which is worse. Favor drops to −3 for whoever did it.
- **He has no hit points.** Nothing at their level can hurt him.

## No innocents aboard

**No innocent creature can be harmed on the Sallowmay.** It's the oldest law of his garden, the guest-law, older than the wager, and the ship carries it with her. Whether something is innocent is always your call.

### Fishing

When someone pulls up a fish (or a crab, or anything else), roll a die to see whether it was a good one or a bad one. A d6 works: **1 to 3, a bad fish; 4 to 6, a good fish.** Change the odds to suit the moment.

- **A bad fish** (a bully of the reef, one that ate its neighbors' eggs) can die, and it can be cooked and eaten.
- **A good fish** won't die and can't be killed, and it shows no sign of pain. The hook slides out without a mark, the knife won't cut, and it flops happily until someone throws it back.

### Food from shore

Meat bought for the ship's account comes only from animals that deserved it. The butcher doesn't know why he picks the ones he does, but he always has a story ready:

> "This pig? Mean as a snake. Bit my boy twice and chased the priest down the lane. Your captain's welcome to him."

### People

The same goes for people. Rescued sailors, a stowaway, a prisoner who has surrendered: no one can hurt them aboard. A blow meant for an innocent turns aside, a rope lets go, a deck plank tilts. Someone attacking the ship isn't innocent, so boarders can be fought as normal.

### Not the crew

**The law protects guests, and the crew aren't guests.** Passengers, rescued sailors, a stowaway, a fish pulled aboard: all guests. When the players took his hire, they signed on as crew, and crew are part of the ship. The ship takes her knocks, and so do they. If anyone asks:

> "You're not my guests. You're my crew. That's a different promise."

If a character ever quits the crew, the protection covers them again, because they're a guest once more.

### As a clue

This is one of the best clues the crew can find on their own: a fish that won't die, a knife that won't cut. If they ask the captain, he answers truthfully: "Nothing that doesn't deserve it comes to harm on my ship." Arcana DC 15 recognizes it as fae guest-law.

## His story

### The Lord of Far Shores

Calandrous Callomaydare was an archfey of the twilight courts, and he loved stories of the mortal world more than anything. He collected them the way other fae collect jewels: every coast, every harbor, every island anyone had ever sung about. He never traveled himself. He didn't need to. He boasted that no shore in the world was hidden from him.

### The wager

Three hundred years ago, at a midsummer revel by the sea, someone old and grey and patient was listening: Mother Brine, the oldest power of the sea, neither cruel nor kind. She offered him a wager. If he could name every island in her sea, she'd give him any one thing he asked. If he couldn't, he would owe her.

He named a thousand islands. She named one he'd never heard of: an island she keeps hidden, that no one has ever charted. He lost.

### The price

- He must sail her sea until **every coast in it has been charted by mortal hands** and given to mortal people.
- Until then, **he can't set foot on land.**
- **He can't draw the maps himself.** Fae ink won't hold a mortal coast; by morning the lines have wandered off the page. So he needs a crew.
- Only **charts made by mortal choice** count. That's why he lets the crew make every decision.

### The Sallowmay

The ship is the last piece of home he brought with him. She was grown, not built, from a willow and a hawthorn in his own garden. Sallow is an old word for willow, and may is the hawthorn's old name. That's why she never needs repairs: she heals. He loves her the way you'd love a dog that has followed you across the world.

### Three hundred years of crews

He has had many crews. Some grew old and went home. Some died, and he couldn't save them without breaking the rule. Some broke their word to him. He has learned to keep a little distance, and to let the crew make the choices, partly because the bargain demands it and partly because it hurts less.

He's quietly delighted by the Guild of Explorers: a whole guild of mortals paid to chart coasts. Every map they file counts toward his debt. It's why he sends his crews to them.

### The hidden island

Here's the catch he doesn't talk about: until the island Mother Brine named is charted, the debt can never be paid. He doesn't know where it is. Your campaign notes already have "a place that isn't on any map" as an island idea. That's this island, and it can be the campaign's ending: the crew finds it, charts it, and sets him free.

### What freedom would mean

He wants to walk on a beach again, feel sand, sit under a tree that isn't a ship. He's afraid he'll miss the sea, and the crew, and he'd never say so.

## The rescue and the reveal

Your notes set this up: if a character dies, he appears beside them out of thin air and brings them back. It's the only time he ever leaves the ship. Now it has a cost that ties into the backstory: **stepping off the Sallowmay breaks the terms of the wager, and Mother Brine takes her due.**

- **His price:** the glamour breaks for good. From then on the crew sees him as he really is. And Mother Brine hides one more island somewhere in her sea, so his debt just got longer (and the crew has a new place to find). He doesn't regret it.
- **The character's price:** as in your notes, a small fae mark, such as a silver mark on the skin or a favor owed. A good one: the revived character can now hear the sea talking, faintly, at night.

Read when he appears:

> The air beside you folds like a sail catching wind, and the captain is there, kneeling on the stones, which he has never once done. Salt water runs from his boots. Where his face was, there's something older: skin with the sheen of the inside of a shell, hair drifting as if underwater, eyes like the deep sea with light far down in it. He lays a hand on your friend's chest and speaks a word you feel in your teeth. Far away, the tide turns.

Then let him say his name, the whole of it, once.

## Hooks to use if you like them

- **Hargrove-Vance and Fontaine.** Maybe they crewed the Sallowmay fifteen years ago, and that's the voyage that "went wrong": Hargrove-Vance broke his word to the captain (sold a chart to someone other than the Guild), and the ship's luck turned on him. It would explain his grudge against the crew, and why Fontaine trusts the captain without understanding him.
- **Two sprites.** Hargrove-Vance's familiar is a sprite too, and his is the real thing: a spirit wearing a sprite's shape, at a warlock's beck and call. Thimble can tell at a glance, and it makes her furious. If the crew ever sees both, a sharp player might notice the difference.
- **The rival's patron.** Hargrove-Vance really is a warlock, sworn to an Unseelie fae (name still to decide) who wants the captain to lose his wager, so the crew must never finish a chart. Thimble may know who it is, and she won't say the name out loud.
- **The firebird.** Caged in cold iron, the one thing he can't touch. He can't go to Lantern Rock, and he won't ask, but he'll be very glad if they free it. The feather glows brighter when he's near.
- **The cathedral bells.** Pip swears they rang by themselves the morning the crew notice went up, and they rang again when the ship left. It's not the captain's doing; it's Mother Brine noticing a new crew.
- **Old crews.** Greta's grandmother might have sailed on the Sallowmay. Ask her about the captain and she says: "Green eyes? My gran used to talk about a captain with green eyes."
- **Payment.** No one ever sees him pay for anything. Merchants find sea-silver in their tills: old coins, salt-crusted, from wrecks no one remembers.
